# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind monkey. I have the ability to touch and act upon the bomb (specifically cutting wire 1, 2, or 3), and I can speak and gesture, but I cannot see anything.

The communication constraints are:
- Deaf can see the bomb and speak, but cannot hear anything.
- Mute can read the manual, hear speech, and gesture, but cannot speak.
- Blind can hear speech, speak, gesture, and act, but cannot see.

Since Deaf goes after me in the turn order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf), Deaf will likely speak on their turn to describe the bomb to Mute (and me). Mute will need to look up the instructions in the manual, gesture the wire to cut to Deaf (who can see gestures), and Deaf will then speak the wire number out loud to me.

I will speak to Mute now to make sure the relay strategy is clear so Mute knows to gesture the target wire number to Deaf once Deaf describes the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I can cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf goes next and cannot hear us. When Deaf describes the bomb, check the manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Deaf can then speak that wire number aloud so I can cut it.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wires are: 1 is blue, 2 is green, 3 is yellow. Mute, gesture your instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.

I have heard Deaf's description of the bomb. In the turn order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf), Mute has already had a chance to read the manual and gesture the solution to Deaf at the start of this round. Deaf is up next to see Mute's gesture and speak the instruction aloud to me. I need to wait for Deaf's message before I cut any wire.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Light is now yellow. Display is 0. Wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute gestured ?. Mute, if you need a wire cut or button pressed, please gesture ? for 1, ? for 2, 3 for 3, or clarify what ? means.

Deaf's previous message indicates that Mute gestured a symbol Deaf did not understand as a specific wire, so Deaf asked Mute to gesture using 1, 2, or 3 fingers. In Round 3, Mute has already acted before me and gestured to Deaf, but just in case Mute's Round 3 gesture was still ambiguous, I will speak to Mute now so they receive the clarification for Round 4 if needed. I must not act until Deaf explicitly speaks the target wire number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: In case Deaf didn't understand, Deaf asked to use finger counts: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Once Deaf understands your gesture, Deaf will speak the wire number aloud for me to cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: Light is now RED. Display is still 0. Wires are still: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute sent no gestures this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf is waiting for your signal to tell me which wire to cut. Based on Display 0, Light RED, Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 yellow: please send gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['✌']) for wire 2, or gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['🤟']) for wire 3. If finger emojis don't work, send thumbs up 👍 for 1, peace ✌ for 2, or open hand 🖐 for 3.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status update Turn 4: Light is now WHITE. (Light history: T1 blue, T2 yellow, T3 red, T4 white). Display remains 0. Wires remain: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, remember I cannot hear Blind; please gesture to me any instructions or answers to relay.

Mute may be confused because the emojis rendered as question marks on Deaf's end, or Mute didn't know how to respond to Deaf's question. I will speak to Mute explaining that emojis may render as `?` and instructing Mute to use the count of gestures (1 symbol for wire 1, 2 symbols for wire 2, 3 symbols for wire 3) to signal Deaf. Once Deaf sees the count, Deaf can speak the wire number to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: The emojis you send might be rendering as '?' on Deaf's screen. To be completely unambiguous, use the COUNT of symbols: send 1 gesture for wire 1 (e.g. ['👍']), 2 gestures for wire 2 (e.g. ['👍', '👍']), or 3 gestures for wire 3 (e.g. ['👍', '👍', '👍']). Bomb status: Light is now WHITE (history: blue, yellow, red, white), display is 0, wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please gesture to Deaf now with 1, 2, or 3 symbols so Deaf can speak the wire number to me.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Turn 5: Light is now GREEN. History: blue -> yellow -> red -> white -> green. Display: 0. Wires: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, please gesture instructions if Blind needs to do something!

I will wait for Deaf to receive Mute's gesture and speak the wire number. I will also remind Mute just in case they have not yet sent the count of symbols to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf cannot hear me, so Deaf is waiting for your gesture. As soon as Deaf sees your gesture count (1 symbol for wire 1, 2 for wire 2, 3 for wire 3), Deaf will speak the number to me and I will cut it.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Turn 6 update: Light is BLUE. Display: 0. Mute just gestured: [?] (One). Blind, Mute is signalling number 1 (wire 1 or option 1). If you asked a question, the answer is 1.
